desc:
A binary watch shows the hour with 4 LEDs worth 8, 4, 2 and 1, and the minute with 6 LEDs worth 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1. The lit LEDs of a group add up to the number it displays.

Exactly turnedOn of the 10 LEDs are lit. Return every time the watch could be showing. A valid hour is 0..11 and a valid minute is 0..59.

Encode each time as the number of minutes since midnight, hour * 60 + minute. The times may be returned in any order, and each time must appear once.
constraints: Hours go from 0 to 11 and minutes from 0 to 59 (a lit pattern that shows 12 or more hours, or 60 or more minutes, is not a time)
hints: There are only 10 LEDs, so you can afford to look at every way of lighting exactly turnedOn of them.
Choose LEDs one at a time in increasing order of position, so that each set is built exactly once. Track the hour value and the minute value as you go.
LEDs 0..3 add 1 << led to the hour, LEDs 4..9 add 1 << (led - 4) to the minute. Both values only grow as you add LEDs, so stop a branch the moment the hour exceeds 11 or the minute exceeds 59.
editorial: Treat the 10 LEDs as items and pick exactly turnedOn of them. Recurse with the index of the next LED allowed, the number of LEDs still to light, and the running hour and minute. Each choice adds a power of two to the hour or to the minute. Because adding more LEDs can never lower either value, a branch whose hour is already above 11 or whose minute is above 59 can be cut immediately. When no LEDs remain to light, record hour * 60 + minute.

A tiny alternative is to loop over all 12 * 60 times and keep the ones whose two bit counts add up to turnedOn. Both are fast here; the backtracking version is the one that generalises to larger watches.
